title: Adaptive cache gauge and tenant quant-reserve: prefill budget governor
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: Tenant cold-batch prefill and cache sizing are primary drivers of unit cost variance. Current defaults are conservative and occasionally over-provision adaptive cache allocations, which increases token cost for low-value tenants. This PR introduces an adaptive cache gauge combined with a tenant-level quant-reserve policy that allocates a small, guaranteed quantization headroom (the "reserve") for tenants during prefill/warmup, plus a telemetry bridge that surfaces decision data to Console and the autotune CLI.

Summary:
- Adaptive cache gauge: runtime component that measures per-tenant prefix hit-rate, recent mini-burst frequency, and effective latency delta; produces a continuous "cache_score" used by the prefill allocator and the batch router.
- Tenant quant-reserve: policy layer allowing operators/tenants to reserve a quantization profile budget (e.g., allow fallback to int8-safe profiles for a percentage of requests) during cold-start periods to preserve SLAs while reducing cost.
- Telemetry bridge: new metrics (prefill.cache_score, prefill.quant_reserve_usage, prefill.reserve_evictions) and a lightweight events export for dry-run simulations.
- Dry-run simulation harness: a CLI-mode that runs the policy against replayed traces and emits a cost/latency delta report.

Review conversation (selected):
- Ethan Park (review): "Nice direction — the gauge looks lightweight. Two asks: 1) add a short-circuit to avoid changes under heavy global load spikes, 2) add a comment explaining the smoothing window rationale."
- Marisol (author): "Added the global-load short-circuit and extended the comments in gauge.go; smoothing window is now configurable per-tenant (defaults in prefill_defaults.yaml)."
- Nora Li (review): "Quant-reserve API surface looks good. Please add an explicit audit log entry when a tenant-level reserve is applied/evicted for compliance."
- Marisol: "Added audit log emit in policy path and a test exercising eviction path."
- Sanjay Patel (review): "Telemetry labels look correct; can we avoid high-cardinality tags for tenant defaults?"
- Marisol: "Switched to tenant_cohort tag and ensured tenant_id is only in event payload, not metric labels."

CI summary:
- unit: pass
- integration (prefill suite): pass after two reruns (flaky network mock fix)
- lint: pass
- e2e (console hooks): pass
- load-sim smoke: pass

Merge: Squash + merge on green; small follow-up hotfix merged for a metrics naming typo.

Why unique: This PR combines a continuous runtime gauge with a policy-driven quant reserve concept and a dry-run simulation path that lets SRE/Customer Success evaluate tenant-level affordability trade-offs before enabling defaults. It emphasizes low-cardinality telemetry, explicit audit hooks for compliance, and a conservative global short-circuit to ensure stability during cluster-wide load spikes.

Deployment notes:
- Defaults are conservative (reserve disabled by default).
- Ops can enable tenant_cohort-level reserves via Console or the prefills CLI.
- Recommended rollout: enable dry-run for 2 weeks, review quant_reserve_usage in Console, then opt-in cohort-by-cohort.

Release notes: "Add adaptive prefill cache gauge and optional tenant quant-reserve policy to reduce warmup unit costs. Includes telemetry and dry-run simulator for safe rollouts."
